Delicious and Friendly
Jan 2022
We enjoyed this place so much we went back twice in two days. This restaurant is located in Nhon Ly village, not Quy Nhon. It seems that a number of visitors to hotels in the area think they were in Quy Nhon city which is about 8 miles away. 

Anyway, this is a fairly large restaurant but is empty due to COVID restrictions. The seafood options were amazing. I am not sure that I agree that the prices were high. If they were, they were not high compared to hotel food at the nearby FLC resort hotels. It's true that the restaurant will pay for your taxi to/from the FLC resorts which are about 4 km on the road or about 1.5 km along the beach - but you do have to go through a bit of water depending on the tide so consider your footwear!

The seafood was incredibly fresh and the staff took such good care of us. And, if you sit by the windows, you have an amazing view of the nearby mountain and pagoda.

One of the better seafood restaurants here, 20 metres from Eo Gio
Jan 2021
Prelude:
Quy Nhon is a small fishing village, so we were afraid we can't find any good restaurants for our short holiday. Thank God the hubs found one on the Vietnamese websites with good reviews. Not much information about it on English/ international platforms.

First look: 
Looks pretty plain from the outside when we arrived in the early evening, and it was still rather empty. Just simple wooden tables and chairs and no air-conditioning in this three-storey building. 

Second look:
However as we finished our dinner, it was rather clear that this was already one of, if not, the biggest restaurant, and the most well-lit one in this area, which is right beside Eo Gio, the main attraction in Quy Nhon. More customers thronged in after 7pm. Large groups of Koreans here for cheap seafood and beer.

Menu:
Surprisingly, they provided us a bilingual "Vietnamese-English" menu. We also saw bilingual "Vietnamese-Chinese" menus. They probably also have Korean ones given the large number of Koreans in the restaurant (small side note: Koreans form the largest expat community in Vietnam). The range of foods available are extensive - from seafood, to snails, to Western, to Vietnamese food, etc.

Recommended:
1. Jellyfish hotpot --- It didn't look like much when it arrived, but boy, did it taste good. Every crunch is amazing. It's caught right here in Quy Nhon.
2. Seaweed soup --- different parts of the oceans produce different types of seaweeds, and the kind that is sold here/ growing here in Quy Nhon is hairy and crunchy!
3. Lobsters, oysters, mussels, many different kinds of clams and (sea) snails --- prices are comparative to those in Ho Chi Minh City, which is alright, considering this is a proper restaurant in a touristy area, and not a roadside stall. For comparison's sake, it is 17,000vnd (~USD0.74) for an oyster of 4-cm diameter. You get to select live lobsters from their tanks, they'll weigh it and let you know how much it'll cost, then you'll get to choose what ways you want it to be cooked. We had it cooked two ways --- grilled with cheese, and the heads with congee/porridge. The warm porridge was so satisfying. It was a supper we never knew we needed, on a cold chilly night in Quy Nhon.

Not recommended:
Their grilled pork ribs. Too dry and tough.

Getting here:
Call them, they'll pick you up from your hotel for free. It's just 5-10 minutes away from most hotels as Quy Nhon is a small town. We did that, and visited Eo Gio 20 metres away before coming back to the restaurant for lunch. We were here for dinner the night before, and they sent us back to our hotel for free too!
